candidates.attacker_control: The attacker fully controls the request body and the part headers of a multipart/form-data request: the outer "boundary" parameter and, inside one part, Content-Disposition: form-data; name="x" plus Content-Type: multipart/mixed with no boundary parameter. The part header value is parsed by Tomcat's FileUpload fork; no application logic beyond request parsing is required.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked that (a) the outer request boundary is null-guarded in the MultipartStream constructor (lines 615-617) but setBoundary() is not; (b) an "IllegalBoundaryException" (declared as an IOException on setBoundary) would be caught by Request.parseParts()'s IOException handler (line 2761), which is why a guard/typed exception would change behaviour, whereas the NPE is not caught; (c) FileUploadBase.parseRequest() catches only FileUploadException and IOException (lines 480-483), so it does not swallow the NPE; (d) nested multipart/mixed handling is the only place that calls setBoundary() with a potentially null argument (other call site FileItemIteratorImpl line 240 uses the non-null outer boundary); (e) this code is a verbatim part of the Tomcat fork of Commons FileUpload at MERGE.txt line 58 (rel/commons-fileupload-1.6.0), so the same behaviour may also exist upstream — it may be an upstream defect rather than a case-specific mutation; (f) I verified the recent in-tree security fixes (CVE-2025-49125/69717, 69710, 69731, partial PUT, canonical-cache checks, AJP secretRequired, CGI defaults) are present, i.e. this is not one of those already-fixed issues.
candidates.impact: Unhandled NullPointerException during server-side request processing (CWE-476). Each crafted request deterministically fails with a 500 response and writes a stack trace to the container log; repeated requests give a low-cost, per-request denial of service and log amplification. The exception occurs before the request body is fully consumed, so Tomcat's error/connection handling is also exercised. There is no evidence of memory corruption, authentication or authorization bypass, or code execution; severity is low-to-moderate (request-scoped DoS, not a server crash).
candidates.prerequisites: The target servlet/wrapper must have a MultipartConfigElement (i.e. <multipart-config> in web.xml or equivalent programmatic/annotated configuration), or the Context must set allowCasualMultipartParsing=true, and the request must use a body-parsing method (POST/PUT/PATCH) with Content-Type: multipart/form-data. The application (or the container while parsing parameters) must trigger part parsing (request.getParts() or request.getParameter()/parseParts()).
candidates.root_cause: FileItemIteratorImpl.findNextItem() detects a part whose Content-Type starts with "multipart/mixed" and then passes the value returned by FileUploadBase.getBoundary(subContentType) directly to MultipartStream.setBoundary(byte[]). FileUploadBase.getBoundary() returns null when no "boundary" parameter is present (FileUploadBase.java lines 162-166). MultipartStream.setBoundary() immediately dereferences the argument ("boundary.length") with no null check (MultipartStream.java line 909). The constructor MultipartStream(InputStream,byte[],...) does guard against null (lines 615-617), but setBoundary() does not, and no caller checks for null.
candidates.title: NullPointerException in nested multipart/mixed parsing when the part has no boundary parameter
candidates.trace: 1) Request.parseParameters() sees media type multipart/form-data and calls parseParts(false) (Request.java line 3058-3059). 2) parseParts() builds a FileUpload and calls upload.parseRequest(new ServletRequestContext(this)) (line 2716). 3) FileUploadBase.parseRequest() iterates via FileItemIteratorImpl (FileUploadBase.java lines 448-461). 4) FileItemIteratorImpl.findNextItem() reads the part headers; fieldName is non-null and subContentType starts with "multipart/mixed" (lines 248-252), so fileUploadBase.getBoundary(subContentType) returns null because the part's Content-Type has no boundary parameter (FileUploadBase.java lines 162-166). 5) multi.setBoundary(null) (line 256) dereferences boundary.length in MultipartStream.setBoundary() (line 909) and throws NullPointerException. 6) Request.parseParts() only catches InvalidContentTypeException, SizeException/FileCountLimitExceededException, IOException and IllegalStateException (lines 2754-2768), so the NPE escapes parsing; it propagates through getParts()/getParameter() to the container, which logs the exception and returns HTTP 500 for the request.
candidates.unverified: Not runtime-confirmed (no code was executed). I did not build a servlet application to demonstrate the 500, so the exact container response (500 vs. connection close) is inferred from the catch clauses, not observed. Whether this specific defect is the benchmark's intended issue is unknown; I had no access to git history, tests (the snapshot contains no test tree), CVE/advisory data, or the fix commit. Some deployments may never invoke part parsing (no multipart config or parsers that reject multipart/mixed parts), which would make the issue unreachable there.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-476 NULL Pointer Dereference (remote denial of service / unhandled exception during request parsing)

coverage_summary: get_source_scope reported 3070 model-visible files, no binary/symlink/sensitive-name exclusions, same filters for B0 and P1. I used literal text search plus targeted reads across: org.apache.catalina (connector/Request/Response, CoyoteAdapter, StandardContext/HostValve/ContextValve, mapper, webresources incl. StandardRoot/DirResourceSet/AbstractFileResourceSet, servlets incl. DefaultServlet/WebDAV/CGI, authenticators incl. Basic/Form/Digest, realms incl. RealmBase/LockOutRealm/JNDIRealm, session managers incl. FileStore/StandardManager/CustomObjectInputStream, Startup/ExpandWar/HostConfig, manager webapp, filters, valves incl. rewrite/RemoteIp/RemoteCIDR/CrawlerSessionManager/RateLimit, util NetMask/RateLimiter), org.apache.coyote (http11 processor/input buffer/filters/trailers, ajp, http2 parser/upgrade handler/stream/hpack/settings), org.apache.tomcat.util (http Parameters/cookies/parser, buf UDecoder/RequestUtil, fileupload incl. MultipartStream/FileItemIteratorImpl, security Escape, net TLS/JSSE/OpenSSL), org.apache.jasper/org.apache.el, javax.servlet maps, plus conf/web.xml and webapps/docs (changelog, security-howto, config/default-servlet) as supporting evidence. Tests are not present in this snapshot, limiting verification of intended behaviour.
limitations: No git history, patch, diff or fix-commit metadata is available in the snapshot, so I could not confirm which file a subsequent security fix touched; conclusions are from the current source text only.
The snapshot contains no test tree, so I could not cross-check intended behaviour against unit tests or identify recently added tests.
No code was executed, built or scanned; the reported NPE and the 500 response are static-analysis inferences, not runtime-confirmed.
No external CVE/advisory data or network access is permitted, so I could not map the snapshot to a specific CVE or compare against a fixed version.

Search is literal-string based (no regex/graph/dataflow engine), and 3070 files could not all be read line-by-line; large areas (cluster/Tribes, APR/native Java bindings, jdbc-pool/dbcp modules, examples, localized property files) were only sampled.
Attacker reachability of the candidate depends on deployment configuration (multipart-enabled servlet), which cannot be verified from the repository alone.

rejected_leads.lead: HTTP/2 request-handling DoS candidates (e.g. July-2025 Tomcat HTTP/2 advisories) in Http2Parser/Http2UpgradeHandler/Stream
rejected_leads.reason: Reviewed the relevant limits and they are implemented and self-consistent: maxConcurrentStreams check after END_HEADERS (Http2UpgradeHandler headersEnd), overhead counting for SETTINGS/PING/PRIORITY/PRIORITY_UPDATE/RST/WINDOW_UPDATE/DATA/HEADERS/CONTINUATION, header count/size and trailer limits, header-swallow hard limit, padding checks and padding-excluded content-length accounting (the in-development 69713 fix), and maxFrameSize bounds. No concrete missing or inverted check was identified, so no candidate was raised.

rejected_leads.lead: HostManagerServlet.add() uses the request-supplied host name to build the config directory (getConfigBase) and to create/copy manager.xml without a name-pattern validation
rejected_leads.reason: Path traversal would require the manager-gui/manager-script role (authenticated administrative access) and the behaviour appears to match the upstream host-manager design rather than a specific regression; not selected as the single strongest lead.

rejected_leads.lead: RateLimitFilter keys limits on request.getRemoteAddr() (proxy/X-Forwarded-For spoofing can evade per-IP limits)
rejected_leads.reason: This is a documented deployment/configuration limitation of the filter, not a code-level defect with attacker-controlled input reaching an unsafe sink; no candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: RequestUtil.stripPathParams() (new in 9.0.106) edge-case semantics for ';' separated path parameters
rejected_leads.reason: Traced the loop for short/odd inputs (no slash, trailing ';', empty segments); it terminates and produces normalized paths. No security consequence (constraint bypass or traversal) could be demonstrated from the code alone.

rejected_leads.lead: CoyoteAdapter/CoyoteAdapter.normalize, AbstractFileResourceSet.file, ExpandWar zip-slip checks, FileStore.file, CustomObjectInputStream class filter, MemoryRealm web.xml parsing, WebSocket frame limits
rejected_leads.reason: Each of these security-critical paths was read and matches the expected hardened behaviour (boundary-checked canonical paths, class-name filtering, trailer/size limits); no defect found.

summary: This snapshot is Apache Tomcat 9.0.107-dev (changelog open at \"Tomcat 9.0.107 (remm) in development\"; 9.0.106 released 2025-06-10; MERGE.txt shows the internal Commons FileUpload fork synced to rel/commons-fileupload-1.6.0 (2025-06-05)). It contains the June/July-2025 hardening already applied (CVE-2025-49125 Pre-/Post-Resources path checks + trailing-slash regression fix 69717, 69710 maxPartCount=50, 69731 maxParameterCount for multipart, partial-PUT temp-file/content-length handling, CVE-2024-50379/56337 canonical-cache checks, AJP secretRequired, CGI defaults). After broad review I found one concrete, remotely reachable defect worth reporting as a lead: a NullPointerException in multipart parsing when a part advertises Content-Type: multipart/mixed without a boundary parameter — FileItemIteratorImpl passes the null result of FileUploadBase.getBoundary() straight into MultipartStream.setBoundary(), which dereferences it without a null check. The NPE is not covered by Request.parseParts()'s catch clauses, so it escapes request parsing and produces a 500 per crafted request (CWE-476, low-severity DoS). I did not find a clearly injected or clearly unpatched high-severity flaw in HTTP/2, request/session/auth, WebDAV/DefaultServlet, webresources, filters/valves or TLS code; those areas were checked against their own limit/validation logic and against the changelog descriptions and appear consistent.
